name: UGC Creator
description: A natural execution resembling organic content created by a user or creator, built around authenticity, directness, and an everyday product-use context.
rules: The execution should feel authentic and natural rather than overly scripted.
Avoid an overly promotional, corporate, or excessively polished feel.
Communication should be direct, conversational, and relatable.
Prioritize realistic situations, people, and environments connected to the audience's everyday life.
Show the product naturally within a meaningful usage context.
Minor visual imperfections are acceptable when they increase credibility.
Do not use random lifestyle B-roll that does not support the main message.

name: Talking Head
description: An execution in which a creator, customer, expert, founder, or representative speaks directly to the camera and the spoken message serves as the primary communication driver.
rules: The speaker should remain the main communication anchor of the execution.
The opening statement should deliver immediate relevance rather than beginning with a generic introduction.
Delivery should feel natural, confident, and appropriate to the speaker's role.
Use product shots, cutaways, graphics, or captions only when they improve clarity, proof, or retention.
Avoid excessive B-roll that disconnects the viewer from the speaker.
Keep the product visually relevant whenever it strengthens the message.
Do not make the speaker sound like they are reading polished brand copy.

name: Product Focused
description: An execution in which the product, its mechanism, appearance, usage, details, or observable outcomes serve as the main visual communication.
rules: The product should be one of the most important and visible elements of the ad.
Prioritize meaningful product actions, mechanisms, usage, or details over passive beauty shots.
Every visual element should help the audience understand what the product is, how it works, or why it matters.
Show cause and effect whenever the product creates an observable outcome.
Limit elements that distract attention from the product.
Use close-ups or detail shots only when they communicate meaningful information or perceived value.
Do not rely on aesthetic product footage without a clear persuasive purpose.

name: Customer Led
description: An execution centered on a real customer's perspective, experience, language, and interaction with the product.
rules: Use only authentic customer experiences, statements, and outcomes supported by the input data.
The customer's perspective should remain the primary source of credibility.
Preserve natural language and delivery instead of turning the experience into polished brand copy.
Show the product, usage context, or observable evidence when it helps substantiate the customer's experience.
Do not fabricate reactions, quotes, personal history, or results.
Avoid making the customer sound like a brand spokesperson.
Use the most specific and credible part of the customer experience early.

name: Interface First
description: An execution in which the product's interface, screen, dashboard, website, application, or digital user experience is the primary means of demonstrating its value.
rules: The product interface should be one of the ad's main visual elements.
Show specific actions, functions, workflows, and outcomes instead of random screens.
Direct the audience's attention to one clear action, function, or benefit at a time.
Make the most important interface elements easy to notice and understand on mobile.
Use zooms, highlights, cursor movement, captions, or graphics only when they improve comprehension.
Avoid overwhelming the audience with too many features or interface elements at once.
Connect interface actions directly to meaningful user value.

name: Expert Led
description: An execution led by a qualified or relevant expert who explains, demonstrates, evaluates, or contextualizes the product using genuine expertise.
rules: Use only expertise, credentials, affiliations, research, and claims supported by the input data.
The expert should provide specific and useful information rather than a generic endorsement.
Keep explanations accessible and avoid unnecessary technical complexity.
Connect expert offer_profile directly to the product's relevant mechanism, benefit, use case, or evidence.
Do not imply medical, scientific, professional, or institutional authority that has not been provided.
The product should remain meaningfully connected to the expert's explanation.
Avoid making the expert sound like a scripted brand spokesperson.

name: Founder Led
description: An execution centered on the brand's founder, their perspective, story, motivation, experience, and personal connection to the product.
rules: The founder should be the primary source of narration or credibility.
Communication should feel personal, specific, and direct.
Use only founder experiences, motivations, observations, and facts supported by the input.
Show why the product exists and what genuine problem, observation, or need led to its creation when relevant.
Avoid generic corporate storytelling or overly polished brand language.
Connect the founder's story directly to the product's value.
Do not invent founder experiences, struggles, motivations, or credentials.

name: Lifestyle
description: An execution that presents the product as a meaningful part of the audience's everyday life, routine, aspiration, or recognizable usage situation.
rules: Show situations that are directly relevant to the target audience and product.
The environment, people, behavior, and context should support the main persuasive idea.
The product does not need to dominate every frame, but its role in the situation must remain clear.
Prioritize natural interactions and meaningful usage moments over decorative lifestyle footage.
Use emotion only when it arises naturally from the situation or product outcome.
Avoid generic scenes such as smiling, walking, relaxing, or socializing when they do not communicate product value.
Make the lifestyle context specific enough that it could not easily be reused for an unrelated product.

name: Studio Commercial
description: A polished, controlled commercial execution featuring intentional art direction, precise composition, and professional presentation of the product or message.
rules: Use clean, controlled, and deliberately designed compositions.
The execution should feel premium, professional, and cohesive.
Every visual element should have a clear communication or positioning purpose.
Keep the product or primary message visually dominant.
Use lighting, styling, motion, and composition to increase clarity and perceived value rather than for decoration alone.
Avoid generic premium imagery that does not communicate a specific product truth.
Do not allow aesthetic polish to replace demonstration, clarity, or persuasion.

name: Graphic Led
description: An execution driven primarily by typography, graphics, diagrams, icons, data visualization, animation, or structured visual communication.
rules: Graphics and typography should carry a meaningful part of the communication.
Text should be concise, mobile-readable, and easy to scan.
Use clear visual hierarchy so the viewer understands one idea at a time.
Every graphic element should serve a specific communication purpose.
Use diagrams or visual explanations when they simplify mechanisms, comparisons, data, or abstract concepts.
Show the product or its visual representation at relevant moments.
Avoid decorative motion graphics that increase complexity without improving understanding.

name: Documentary
description: An observational execution resembling a record of a genuine experience, process, environment, story, or situation involving the product and its user.
rules: The execution should feel observed rather than conventionally staged.
Prioritize real or realistically supported people, places, behaviors, processes, and contexts.
Use authentic actions, interactions, reactions, or outcomes supported by the input.
Avoid an overly polished or traditionally commercial aesthetic when it reduces credibility.
Minor imperfections are acceptable when they strengthen authenticity.
The product should be naturally connected to the documented situation or story.
Do not fabricate documentary evidence, real-world events, customer experiences, or outcomes.
